text:
BERT4Rec originally uses masked-item full-softmax training; a positive-plus-64-negative cross-entropy is a different candidate objective, not automatically an unbiased full-softmax approximation. Uniform sampling supports replacement or uniqueness, and samplers do not necessarily exclude targets automatically ([TensorFlow documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/random/uniform_candidate_sampler)). Algebraically, retaining a negative m times contributes m·exp(score) to the denominator—equivalent to adding log(m) to that item's logit. Thus 64 draws can contain fewer than 64 distinct competitors; deduplicating afterward changes the objective. Importance-corrected sampled softmax requires sampling-aware corrections; plain candidate CE should be described explicitly ([sampled-softmax documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/sampled_softmax_loss)).

Recommended implementation: define each user's eligible negatives as real catalog items excluding all known training positives, including masked targets; exclude padding and the reserved mask token. This is an unseen-item training choice, not original BERT4Rec's full-softmax objective. Never consult held-out labels for exclusions. Sample uniformly without replacement with K=min(64, eligible_count); use all eligible items when fewer exist, mask unused candidate slots to −∞, and skip examples with no eligible negatives. These safeguards prevent accidental target negatives, duplicate weighting and unbounded rejection loops.

For memory efficiency, gather only supervised masked hidden states before the output head—the original implementation already gathers masked positions ([BERT4Rec source](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py)). Implementation inference: for M supervised positions, score only their positive-plus-K candidates, producing M×(K+1) logits instead of B×L×catalog_size. Chunk candidate embedding lookup/scoring to bound the M×K×hidden_dim intermediate; weight chunk losses by supervised-position count so chunking preserves the objective. Keep masked-target inputs and appended-mask inference unchanged.
